what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1959?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1959 annual town report prints no wage list: the whole text (116 pages) was searched for wage, salary, payroll and gross and found only aggregates (the Treasurer's payments by department, p22-25; the accountant's wage lines, p26-36; the voted salaries, p58-59) and the School Personnel list (p103-106), which names staff, education and years of experience and prints no pay (sources/data/report-tables/1959/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1959 payroll register (totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's salary grades and step rates in 1959?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1959 report prints each elected officer's voted salary in the budget (p58-59) and no classification or salary schedule: the whole text was searched for classification (one hit, the accountant's schedule title, p26 and the index p114) and `salary schedule` (no hit) (sources/data/report-tables/1959/). — closes: the Town's 1959 pay plan, if one existed, from the Selectmen's records.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in 1959, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1959 report prints the Machinery Fund as a receipts line (p20) and a receipts-reserved balance (p16 `Highway Machinery` 12,016.09), the school lunch and athletic accounts inside the School Department's own reports (p111, p113), and no town-wide schedule by fund. Searched `revolving` and `special revenue`: no hit (sources/data/report-tables/1959/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1959 fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in 1959?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1959 report prints no such schedule: the special articles carry their balance in the accountant's schedule (p26-36) and in the balance sheet (p16, unexpended balances), and the Selectmen's text (p50) says only that a six-year capital outlay program is coming. Searched `capital`: p50 and p96 (the latter a spelling test) (sources/data/report-tables/1959/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1959 ledger of the building and highway projects.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for 1959?
why: `report-valuation` holds the valuation and levy history from the 1987-2010 reports. The 1959 report prints the assessed valuation as one line of the opening facts page (p4: $9,084,720.00 = real estate $8,690,820.00 + personal property $393,900.00; tax rate $68.80), the State valuation 1945-1959 in the School Committee statistics (p102: $2,703,772.00, a figure that does not match the Assessors' and is not explained), and the overlay only as a reserve (p17) and a funding source (p16, p59). No recapitulation of the levy or of growth; searched valuation, overlay, tax rate and `new growth` (sources/data/report-tables/1959/). — closes: the Assessors' 1959 tax rate recapitulation filed with the State.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1959, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and `report-fee-schedule` the fee per device from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1959 report gives the year's total in prose on p42-43 (`One hundred and seventy weighing and measuring devices were adjusted and sealed`, a net cost to the Town of $427.22) and the Treasurer's receipts one line, `Sealer's Fees` $98.50 (p21), with no count or fee by device type. Searched `sealer` and `weights and measures` (sources/data/report-tables/1959/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1959 test and fee record.

what: What did each Trust Fund Commission fund take in as interest and pay out in 1959?
why: `report-trust-funds` rollforward families hold interest received and transfers by fund in the 1971 and later reports. The 1959 report prints each fund's year-end balance by named bequest (p17, $67,521.92 in all) and the receipts lines `Income` and `Transfer of Funds` by fund (p20), with no roll-forward of opening balance, interest, withdrawals and closing balance. Searched `trust fund` (p5, p20, p24, p36, p57-58, p114) (sources/data/report-tables/1959/). — closes: the Trust Fund Commissioners' 1959 report.
